subject: CS
title: Computer Science Orientation
description: Introduction to Computer Science as a field and career for incoming first year and external transfer students in the computer science majors. Overview of the field and specific examples of problem areas and methods of solution.
notes: UIUC: Optional course, highly recommended, Free Elective; its hour counts as a free elective.

matches.match_rationale: A 1-hour introduction to computer science as a field and career for new CS majors (optional, counted as a free elective).

subject: CS
title: Introduction to Computer Science I
description: Basic concepts in computing and fundamental techniques for solving computational problems. Intended as a first course for computer science majors and others with a deep interest in computing. Credit is not given for both CS 124 and CS 125.
prerequisites: Three years of high school mathematics or MATH 112.

matches.match_rationale: The first computing course for CS majors: basic concepts and techniques for solving computational problems.

subject: MATH
title: MATH 221 or MATH 220 (Calculus I)
description: A first calculus course: limits, derivatives and their applications, and an introduction to integrals. Some universities offer a faster version for students who saw calculus in high school and a longer one for students who did not.
notes: Student chooses one: Calculus I | Calculus. UIUC: MATH 220 is for students with no calculus background; 4 of its 5 hours count toward the degree.

matches.match_rationale: Both options are a first calculus course (MATH 220 for students without calculus background).

subject: ENG
title: Grainger Engineering Orientation Seminar
description: Introduces students to the Grainger College of Engineering and their respective departments. Students will explore the academic environment at Illinois, developing skills that will aid in learning both inside and outside the classroom, build their leadership and collaborative skills, and build community inside and outside the classroom. Through class discussion and assignments, students will explore campus resources, examine and set goals for academic, personal, and professional development, and develop skills to work in diverse teams through a class project.
notes: External transfer students take ENG 300 instead.

matches.match_rationale: A 1-hour orientation to the Grainger College of Engineering and academic life, not CS content.

title: Science Elective
description: A natural science course chosen from an approved list, such as chemistry, biology, astronomy, or geology, in addition to the program's required physics.
notes: UIUC: one course from the Natural Science & Technology list, in addition to PHYS 211 and 212 (exceptions: ASTR 100, PHYS 101/102, CHEM 101).

matches.match_rationale: One natural science course from an approved list, beyond the required physics.

title: Composition I
description: A first-year writing course on academic reading, argument, research, and revision. Students write for different audiences and purposes.
notes: UIUC's semester 1 reads 'Composition I or General Education (choose a Humanities or Social/Behavioral Science course)' (4 hours) and semester 2 'General Education (...) or Composition I course' (3 hours): Composition I goes in one semester and a gen-ed course in the other. Placed here because Composition I is 4-6 hours and gen-ed courses are 3.

matches.match_rationale: A gen-ed writing slot; its content is first-year composition, but as a choice from a list it maps to the gen-ed slot (as with OSU's and Berkeley's writing slots).

subject: CS
title: Introduction to Computer Science II
description: Continuation of CS 124. More advanced concepts in computing and techniques and approaches for solving computational problems.

matches.match_rationale: The continuation of CS 124, with more advanced programming concepts.

subject: CS
title: Discrete Structures
description: Discrete mathematical structures frequently encountered in the study of Computer Science. Sets, propositions, Boolean algebra, induction, recursion, relations, functions, and graphs. Credit is not given toward graduation for: Credit is not given for both CS 173 and MATH 213.
prerequisites: One of CS 124, CS 125, ECE 220; one of MATH 220, MATH 221.

matches.match_rationale: Sets, logic, Boolean algebra, induction, recursion, relations, functions, and graphs.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus II
description: Second course in calculus and analytic geometry: techniques of integration, conic sections, polar coordinates, and infinite series.

matches.match_rationale: Second course in calculus.

title: General Education course (Humanities or Social/Behavioral Science, Cultural Studies)
description: A general education course in the humanities or social and behavioral sciences that also meets a cultural studies requirement, such as non-Western, US minority, or Western and comparative cultures.
notes: UIUC general education: Humanities & the Arts (6 hours), Social & Behavioral Sciences (6 hours), and one course in each of three Cultural Studies categories; Advanced Composition (3 hours) is also required and not placed in the plan.

matches.match_rationale: A humanities or social science gen-ed course that also meets a cultural studies category.

title: General Education course (Humanities or Social/Behavioral Science)
description: A general education course in the humanities, arts, or social and behavioral sciences, chosen from an approved list. These courses add breadth outside engineering and computing.
notes: UIUC's semester 1 reads 'Composition I or General Education (choose a Humanities or Social/Behavioral Science course)' (4 hours) and semester 2 'General Education (...) or Composition I course' (3 hours): Composition I goes in one semester and a gen-ed course in the other. Placed here because Composition I is 4-6 hours and gen-ed courses are 3.

matches.match_rationale: A humanities or social science gen-ed course.

subject: CS
title: Software Design Lab
description: Design and implementation of novel software solutions. Problem identification and definition; idea generation and evaluation; and software implementation, testing, and deployment. Emphasizes software development best practices—including framework selection, code review, documentation, appropriate library usage, project management, continuous integration and testing, and teamwork.
prerequisites: CS 128; credit or concurrent registration in CS 225. Restricted to majors in Computer Science undergraduate curricula only.

matches.match_rationale: A 1-hour team project lab on building software with professional practices (code review, testing, continuous integration); partial because it is a short lab, not a full project course.

subject: CS
title: Data Structures
description: Data abstractions: elementary data structures (lists, stacks, queues, and trees) and their implementation using an object-oriented programming language. Solutions to a variety of computational problems such as search on graphs and trees. Elementary analysis of algorithms. Credit is not given toward graduation for: CS 277 if credit for CS 225 has been earned.
prerequisites: CS 126 or CS 128 or ECE 220; One of CS 173, CS 413, MATH 213, MATH 314, MATH 347, MATH 412, or MATH 413.

matches.match_rationale: Elementary data structures (lists, stacks, queues, trees) and their implementation in an object-oriented language.

subject: MATH
title: Calculus III
description: Third course in calculus and analytic geometry including vector analysis: Euclidean space, partial differentiation, multiple integrals, line integrals and surface integrals, the integral theorems of vector calculus. Credit is not given toward graduation for: Credit is not given for both MATH 241 and MATH 292.

matches.match_rationale: Vector analysis, partial derivatives, multiple and line integrals.

subject: PHYS
title: University Physics: Mechanics
description: Newton's Laws, work and energy, static properties and fluids, oscillations, transverse waves, systems of particles, and rotations. A calculus-based approach for majors in engineering, mathematics, physics and chemistry. Credit is not given toward graduation for: Credit is not given for both PHYS 211 and PHYS 101.
prerequisites: Credit or concurrent registration in MATH 231.

matches.match_rationale: Required calculus-based mechanics; a named science fills the science requirement.
matches.notes: Course row mapped to a slot concept (allowed for lab-science only; decided in step 10).

title: General Education course (Humanities or Social/Behavioral Science, Cultural Studies)
description: A general education course in the humanities or social and behavioral sciences that also meets a cultural studies requirement, such as non-Western, US minority, or Western and comparative cultures.
notes: UIUC general education: Humanities & the Arts (6 hours), Social & Behavioral Sciences (6 hours), and one course in each of three Cultural Studies categories; Advanced Composition (3 hours) is also required and not placed in the plan.

matches.match_rationale: A humanities or social science gen-ed course that also meets a cultural studies category.

subject: CS
title: Computer Architecture
description: Fundamentals of computer architecture: digital logic design, working up from the logic gate level to understand the function of a simple computer; machine-level programming to understand implementation of high-level languages; performance models of modern computer architectures to enable performance optimization of software; hardware primitives for parallelism and security.
prerequisites: CS 125 or CS 128; CS 173 or MATH 213; credit or concurrent enrollment in CS 225.

matches.match_rationale: Machine-level programming, how a simple computer works, and performance; partial because it also covers digital logic.
Starts from logic gates and builds up to a simple computer; partial because logic design is one part of an architecture course.

subject: CS
title: Probability & Statistics for Computer Science
description: Introduction to probability theory and statistics with applications to computer science. Topics include: visualizing datasets, summarizing data, basic descriptive statistics, conditional probability, independence, Bayes theorem, random variables, joint and conditional distributions, expectation, variance and covariance, central limit theorem. Markov inequality, Chebyshev inequality, law of large numbers, Markov chains, simulation, the PageRank algorithm, populations and sampling, sample mean, standard error, maximum likelihood estimation, Bayes estimation, hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, linear regression, principal component analysis, classification, and decision trees. Credit is not given toward graduation for: Credit is not given for both CS 361 and ECE 313.
prerequisites: MATH 220 or MATH 221. Credit or concurrent registration in one of MATH 225, MATH 227, MATH 257, MATH 415, MATH 416, ASRM 406 or BIOE 210.

matches.match_rationale: Probability and statistics for computer science: data summaries, conditional probability, random variables, and inference.

subject: MATH
title: Linear Algebra with Computational Applications
description: Introductory course incorporating linear algebra concepts with computational tools, with real world applications to science, engineering and data science. Topics include linear equations, matrix operations, vector spaces, linear transformations, eigenvalues, eigenvectors, inner products and norms, orthogonality, linear regression, equilibrium, linear dynamical systems and the singular value decomposition. Credit is not given for both MATH 257 and any of MATH 125, MATH 225, MATH 227, MATH 415 or ASRM 406.
notes: UIUC's requirements also allow MATH 415 or MATH 416 for this course.
prerequisites: MATH 220 or MATH 221; CS 101 or equivalent programming experience.

matches.match_rationale: Linear equations, matrices, vector spaces, eigenvalues, orthogonality, and the SVD, with computation.

subject: PHYS
title: University Physics: Elec & Mag
description: Coulomb's Law, electric fields, Gauss' Law, electric potential, capacitance, circuits, magnetic forces and fields, Ampere's law, induction, electromagnetic waves, polarization, and geometrical optics. A calculus-based approach for majors in engineering, mathematics, physics, and chemistry. Credit is not given toward graduation for: Credit is not given for both PHYS 212 and PHYS 102.
prerequisites: PHYS 211; credit or concurrent registration in MATH 241.

matches.match_rationale: Required calculus-based electricity and magnetism; part of the named physics requirement.
matches.notes: Course row mapped to a slot concept (allowed for lab-science only; decided in step 10).

title: Free Elective
description: Any course the student chooses, inside or outside the major, that counts toward the degree. Students often use free electives for a minor, extra courses in the major, or personal interests.
notes: UIUC: additional course work, subject to the Grainger College of Engineering restrictions on free electives, to reach 128 hours.

matches.match_rationale: Any course counting toward the degree, within the college's restrictions.

subject: CS
title: CS 210 or CS 211 (Ethical & Professional Issues)
description: A short course on ethics and professional conduct in computing, covering topics such as privacy, intellectual property, security, and professional responsibility.
notes: Student chooses one: Ethical & Professional Issues | Ethical and Professional Conduct.

matches.match_rationale: Both options are ethics and professional conduct for computing.

subject: CS
title: System Programming
description: Basics of system programming, including POSIX processes, process control, inter-process communication, synchronization, signals, simple memory management, file I/O and directories, shell programming, socket network programming, RPC programming in distributed systems, basic security mechanisms, and standard tools for systems programming such as debugging tools. Credit is not given for both CS 341 and either CS 241 or ECE 391.

matches.match_rationale: POSIX processes, synchronization, memory management, file I/O, and network programming, taught as systems programming; partial because it is not an OS internals course (as with UIC's CS 361).

subject: CS
title: Numerical Methods I
description: Fundamentals of numerical methods for students in science and engineering; floating-point computation, systems of linear equations, approximation of functions and integrals, the single nonlinear equation, and the numerical solution of ordinary differential equations; various applications in science and engineering; programming exercises and use of high quality mathematical library routines. (Counts for advanced hours in LAS). Same as MATH 357. Credit is not given toward graduation for: Credit is not given towards graduation for CS 357 if credit for CS 450 has been earned.
prerequisites: One of CS 101, CS 105, CS 124, CS 125 or ECE 220; MATH 241; one of MATH 225, MATH 227, MATH 257, MATH 415, MATH 416, ASRM 406 or BIOE 210.

matches.match_rationale: Floating-point computation, linear systems, approximation, nonlinear equations, and ODEs; no existing concept fits, so it creates numerical-methods.

title: CS Technical Elective
description: An advanced computer science course chosen by the student from an approved list. Common options cover areas such as machine learning, security, graphics, networking, databases, and software engineering.
notes: UIUC: at least six technical electives (18 hours) from CS 397 and the CS 400-level courses, with at least one course in each of several focus areas.

matches.match_rationale: CS 397 and CS 400-level courses with breadth across focus areas.

title: Language Other Than English (3rd level)
description: A third-semester course in a language other than English, or the equivalent proficiency. Students with enough high school study or a placement result may already meet the requirement.
notes: UIUC language requirement: completion of the third semester of a language other than English (0-15 hours, depending on high school study or placement).

matches.match_rationale: A language requirement to the third-semester level; no existing slot fits (gen-ed-elective is a breadth list), so it creates world-language.

subject: CS
title: Introduction to Algorithms & Models of Computation
description: Analysis of algorithms, major paradigms of algorithm design including recursive algorithms, divide-and-conquer algorithms, dynamic programming, greedy algorithms, and graph algorithms. Formal models of computation including finite automata and Turing machines. Limitations of computation arising from fundamental notions of algorithm and from complexity-theoretic constraints. Reductions, undecidability and NP-completeness. Same as ECE 374.

matches.match_rationale: Algorithm analysis and design paradigms (divide and conquer, dynamic programming, greedy, graph algorithms); partial because the course also covers models of computation.
Formal models of computation (automata, Turing machines) and decidability; partial because the course also covers algorithms.

subject: CS
title: Programming Languages & Compilers
description: Structure of programming languages and their implementation. Basic language design principles; abstract data types; functional languages; type systems; object-oriented languages. Basics of lexing, parsing, syntax-directed translation, semantic analysis, and code generation. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 or 4 graduate hours.
prerequisites: One of CS 233, CS 240, CS 340 or ECE 391; CS 374 or ECE 374; one of MATH 225, MATH 257, MATH 415, MATH 416, ASRM 406, or BIOE 210.

matches.match_rationale: Language design principles, types, and functional and object-oriented languages, plus the basics of compilers (lexing, parsing, code generation).

title: CS Advanced Elective
description: An additional advanced course chosen by the student, usually in computer science or a closely related technical field, beyond the required technical electives.
notes: UIUC: at least two advanced electives (6 hours), taken for a letter grade, distinct from the technical electives.

matches.match_rationale: Two advanced courses beyond the technical electives; not limited to CS, so it maps to the broader technical-elective slot.
